title: a-stale-loop-restarts-itself
intention: A stale ground loop restarts itself rather than firing indefinitely against code newer than its own process.
why: The trouble ground-loop-is-older-than-the-code-it-judges has count=207, firing every ~9s since 2026-08-18. The DETECTION is PROVED (staleness-is-about-this-process-not-about-disk); the RESPONSE does not exist. The loop names its own staleness and blames nobody else, correctly — but it keeps running stale, accumulating trouble records, and holding modules that no longer match their files. This ticket is the response: the condition becomes transient because a stale loop restarts.
traces_to: Law 7 — errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces: a stale loop firing 207 times is an error that was loud but not acted on
Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics: auto-restart is physics, not a policy to remember

falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: (1) a code change lands (any .py under cairn/ touched after process_started()) and the loop does NOT exit within one beat cycle after detecting it, unless COMMAND_DO_NOT_RESTART.flag is active in the signal folder — the core property; (2) COMMAND_EXIT.flag in the signal folder and the loop does NOT exit within one beat cycle — the shutdown channel; (3) COMMAND_DO_NOT_RESTART.flag active and a code change detected, and the loop exits ANYWAY — the development hold; (4) the flags/ directory is missing a flag that the code checks — the menu is incomplete; (5) a flag check takes longer than 1ms (two stat calls on the signal folder per beat) — cost creep into the beat; (6) the trouble ground-loop-is-older-than-the-code-it-judges STILL fires after this build ships — the whole point, and the proof is running the loop, landing a code change, and verifying restart. WRONG INTENT if the flag mechanism becomes anything more than presence-based zero-byte files, or if the check examines anything beyond the signal folder per beat (scanning the flags/ menu on every beat wastes the distinction between definition and signal).
